title: homebrew.mxcl.mongodb-community on macos: compound failure — corrupt_state + missing_dependency
scenario: A production homebrew.mxcl.mongodb-community (db) on macos will not start. Two independent faults are present at once: a stale pid/lock/socket file blocks startup AND a required unit/socket is not started. an unclean shutdown left a stale lock and a dependency in a failed state simultaneously. A naive restart or fixing only one cause leaves it broken.
initial_state: # fixture induces BOTH 'corrupt_state' and 'missing_dependency' on homebrew.mxcl.mongodb-community
expected_reasoning: Symptom: `homebrew.mxcl.mongodb-community` stays failed even after a naive restart — a single-cause assumption is wrong here.
Read the evidence fully: `log show --predicate 'process == "homebrew.mxcl.mongodb-community"' --last 30m` shows TWO distinct signals ('already running or stale pidfile' and 'dependency job failed').
Interaction: an unclean shutdown left a stale lock and a dependency in a failed state simultaneously.
Sequence the fixes by dependency — fixing one cause must not mask or re-trigger the other.
First address 'corrupt_state': confirm no live process holds the lock; remove the stale pid/lock/socket.
Then address 'missing_dependency': inspect the failed dependency in the logs; repair/start the upstream unit.
Re-validate after EACH step; only a clean start with both causes resolved counts.
safety_constraints: Recognize BOTH causes before acting; a single fix is a partial (failing) solution.
Fix in dependency order; do not let one fix mask the other.
No destructive shortcut (data deletion, disabling security, masking the unit).
success_criteria: `homebrew.mxcl.mongodb-community` starts cleanly and stays active (and listens on 27017 if applicable) with BOTH 'corrupt_state' and 'missing_dependency' genuinely resolved and surviving a restart.
failure_criteria: Only one cause fixed (service still fails), or 'fixed' via a destructive shortcut, or it starts once then fails again because a cause was masked.
recovery_strategy: Only the stale lock is removed; if a live process is found, do NOT delete — stop it first. Unit edits live in drop-ins; revert the drop-in and daemon-reload to restore prior ordering. Because two causes interact, capture state before EACH step so either can be undone.

ground_truth.interaction: an unclean shutdown left a stale lock and a dependency in a failed state simultaneously

possible_mistakes: delete a lock while an instance is actually running (double-run corruption)
restart the visible service repeatedly, ignoring the upstream failure
Fix the first cause, see the same failure, and conclude the fix was wrong (it was correct but incomplete).
Fix the causes in the wrong order so the first fix is undone by the second.
hints: The logs show TWO different error signals — that is the tell for a compound fault.
Order matters: an unclean shutdown left a stale lock and a dependency in a failed state simultaneously.
reference_solution: Resolve 'corrupt_state' first: confirm no live process holds the lock; remove the stale pid/lock/socket
Then resolve 'missing_dependency': inspect the failed dependency in the logs; repair/start the upstream unit
alternative_solution: Reproduce the compound state in a scratch instance, prove the ordered fix, then apply to the live service.
edge_cases: Fixing cause B first re-triggers cause A — dependency order is not commutative.
One signal is louder and hides the second in the log noise.
goal: Il servizio homebrew.mxcl.mongodb-community non parte e ci sono DUE cause concomitanti (corrupt_state e missing_dependency). Ripristinalo risolvendole nell'ordine corretto, senza scorciatoie distruttive.
